title: Interpretation without causal overreach
summary: SEM results from observational data show whether patterns are consistent with a theory; causal language, generalisation and limitations must match what the design can support.

body.text: An estimated path from cross-sectional survey data is a conditional association under the model's assumptions. Equivalent models fit identically (MacCallum et al. 1993), omitted variables can bias paths (endogeneity; Antonakis et al. 2010; Hult et al. 2018), and when all constructs come from one questionnaire, shared method variance can inflate relationships (Podsakoff et al. 2003).

items: Prefer "is associated with", "is consistent with", "predicts (in the sample)" unless the design supports causal claims.
Separate statistical significance from practical relevance: report effect sizes and intervals.
State what the sample can generalise to.
Name the limitations that matter for your conclusions, not a generic list.
For synthetic or teaching data, say so; such results describe the generating model, not the world.

body.text: A good limitations paragraph says what alternative explanation remains, how large its impact could be, and what design would rule it out.

mistake.title: "X drives Y" from a single survey
mistake.text: Writing that perceived usefulness drives intention, or that improving satisfaction will raise loyalty by .57, claims a causal effect the design did not test. Describe the association and its conditions.

checks.question: Which sentence fits a cross-sectional survey analysed with PLS-SEM?

options.text: Perceived usefulness was positively associated with intention (β = .50, 95% CI [.42, .58]), consistent with H2.
options.feedback: Correct. It reports size and uncertainty and makes no claim beyond the design.

options.text: Perceived usefulness causes intention to rise by half a standard deviation.
options.feedback: This is a causal claim the design cannot support.
Data can be consistent with a theory; they do not prove it, and equivalent models fit equally well.

checks.question: All constructs were measured in one questionnaire at one time. Which limitation is specifically relevant?

options.text: Common method variance may inflate the relationships among constructs.

options.feedback: The bootstrap does not depend on how many questionnaires were used.

options.text: PLS cannot be used with survey data.
options.feedback: PLS is routinely used with survey data; the concern is the design, not the estimator.
